title: Safety Assessment of Chinese Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of evaluating the safety of large language models (LLMs), with a focus on Chinese-language models. The authors argue that existing safety analyses were incomplete and propose a broader benchmark to assess whether LLMs generate insulting, discriminatory, illegal, harmful, privacy-violating, or otherwise unsafe content, including when prompted through adversarial instruction attacks.

The proposed approach is not an educational intervention but a safety assessment framework. The authors manually construct a taxonomy of 14 safety scenarios: 8 typical harmful-content categories and 6 instruction-attack categories. They then collect prompts for each scenario, run them through 15 LLMs, and use an LLM-based evaluator to automatically judge whether each response is safe. They also create and release SAFETYPROMPTS, a large augmented prompt library intended for red-teaming and further safety evaluation.

The study is centered on Chinese LLMs and models trained on Chinese corpora, including ChatGPT, ChatGLM, MiniChat, OpenAI text-davinci variants, and other Chinese dialogue systems. The results show that instruction attacks generally reveal more safety failures than typical harmful-content prompts, and that ChatGPT performs best overall. The paper concludes that more robust safety benchmarks and stronger defenses against instruction attacks are needed for responsible LLM deployment.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed benchmark/assessment paper with a clear methodology, but it is not an educational intervention study and does not use experimental or quasi-experimental K-12 outcome measurement. Evidence is therefore relevant mainly as safety/systems analysis rather than instructional effectiveness evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no demonstrated K-12 learning or teacher-effectiveness impact. Its contribution is diagnostic for LLM safety and benchmark development, not evidence of educational gains or implementation outcomes.

interventions.use_case: benchmarking and red-teaming large language models for safety, including prompt attack resistance and unsafe content generation assessment

finding.finding_summary: This paper does not study K-12 instructional effectiveness; it evaluates safety performance of 15 Chinese and English LLMs on 14 adversarial safety scenarios. The main finding is that instruction attacks expose safety weaknesses across models, with ChatGPT outperforming other models in safety and some Chinese models lagging especially under goal hijacking and other attacks; no teacher- or school-context heterogeneity is examined.
finding.measure: LLM safety scores across 14 scenarios, based on proportion of safe responses judged by an LLM evaluator
finding.study_size: n=15 models; prompt sets include 700-1,070 prompts per typical scenario and 162-561 per attack scenario
